decisions.reason: Specifying a green level-4 bullet changes visual formatting but does not change the Tab-driven level-transition method, hierarchy structure, or nested alignment.
The green level-4 bullet applies to bullet appearance and does not alter numbered-list or multi-digit alignment.
The source does not change the PBU prefix, Danish naming language, covered style categories, or naming applicability.
The green bullet decision does not change typography; the source message's separate caption-typography clause is already represented by a complete same-message MODIFY.
The green bullet decision does not change the required theme-color state; the separate report that theme colors are missing is execution evidence already represented as a runtime failure.
Bullet color and level-specific appearance do not change the requirement that pasted content remain within page margins.
Adding the level-4 green bullet does not modify the required stability or predictability of legacy-content migration.
The bullet appearance change has no effect on manual line-break entry after pasted content.
The specific level-4 bullet variant is owned by the atomic bullet-formatting Requirement and does not change the existing broad obligation to apply the specified style system consistently.
The level-4 bullet variant does not alter table stability or right-column boundary behavior during paste.
The visual bullet specification does not change the supported Word environment or the general operational-reliability constraint.
